papers.title: Probing $τ$ lepton dipole moments at multi-TeV muon colliders
papers.summary: We investigate the sensitivity of future multi-TeV muon colliders to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the $τ$ lepton within the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We consider $τ^+τ^-$ production through $μ^+μ^-$ annihilation and vector-boson scattering, electroweak-boson-associated $τ$ production, and the radiative Higgs decay $H\toτ^+τ^-γ$. At high energies, the dipole-induced contributions quadratic in the Wilson coefficients become particularly important, with associated Higgs production, $μ^+μ^-\toτ^+τ^-H$, providing the strongest sensitivity through energy-enhanced contact interactions. The remaining channels offer complementary probes of the underlying dipole operators. For a $10$~TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of $10\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, we obtain combined sensitivities at the nominal $95\%$ confidence level of $|Δa_τ|<1.2\times10^{-5}$, $|d_τ|<6.6\times10^{-20}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$, $|Δa_τ^Z|<1.8\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_τ^Z|<1.0\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$. Compared with FCC-ee projections, the muon collider offers substantially stronger sensitivity to the electric dipole moments, while both facilities offer complementary probes of magnetic dipole moments. These results motivate further studies incorporating realistic detector effects and systematic uncertainties.

papers.title: Plugging the Pion Chimney
papers.summary: Heavy QCD axions and other gluon-coupled axion-like particles (ALPs) with masses from MeV to GeV are well motivated and have been searched for extensively. However, a window around the neutral pion mass, the so-called pion chimney, has escaped every search. There the ALP mixes strongly with the $π^0$ and therefore shares its experimental signatures. We show that the chimney can be closed with existing LHC data. The key point is that mixing changes the lifetimes of the two mass eigenstates but does not make them equal, and at LHC energies the states are boosted enough for the lifetime to decide whether they escape the detector or decay inside it. The ATLAS monojet search constrains the first case and the ATLAS inclusive photon measurement the second, and together they exclude the chimney up to the cutoff of the ALP effective theory. Above the cutoff, LHC searches for the colored states of the simplest ultraviolet completions exclude the rest. We also show that the bound from the $K^+$ width does not reach the chimney, because an ALP passes the same selection as a $π^0$, and we derive an independent, purely kinematic constraint from the measured $π^\pm$-$π^0$ mass splitting.

papers.title: Feebly-Interacting Particle Searches
papers.summary: In the last several years, feebly-interacting particles (FIPs) have moved from "exotica" to the mainstream of particle physics. This development is fueled by three motivations: FIPs are one of two broad possibilities for new particles, FIPs are as well motivated by dark matter as WIMPs, and FIPs are connected to important problems in particle physics. I review these motivations and then briefly highlight recent progress in a few areas, including axion-like particles, dark photons and other gauge bosons, the X17 anomaly, quirks, and the Forward Physics Facility.
papers.comments: 10 pages, to appear in the Proceedings of ICHEP 2026, the 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics, Natal, Brazil, 30 July to 5 August 2026

papers.title: Unraveling QCD dynamics via charm-tagged jets with ALICE at the LHC
papers.summary: The study of jet substructure provides tests of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and offers differential ways to study hadronization mechanisms. QCD predicts that jet radiation patterns depend on the mass and color charge of the initiating parton. Parton showers are sensitive to the different Casimir factors of quarks and gluons, and to the parton mass through the dead-cone effect. In this talk, we present three sets of $\textrm{D}^0$-meson-tagged jet measurements. First, we present the first measurement of the Energy-Energy Correlator (EEC) for $\textrm{D}^0$-meson-tagged jets. This observable reveals the detailed structure of QCD radiation from heavy quarks, allowing for a distinction between perturbative and non-perturbative effects in charm-quark showers. We then discuss measurements of the angular differences between three different axis definitions inside the jets. The three definitions offer different sensitivity to wide-angle soft radiation and systematically probe the radiation pattern from charm quarks. The final measurement regards jet angularities, which characterize the weighted angular distribution of the jet constituents. These powerful observables probe the parton shower, with sensitivity to parton-mass and Casimir-factor related effects that can be tuned by adjusting the importance of wide-angle radiation.

papers.title: A Reinforcement Learning Method to Navigate SMEFT Operator Space
papers.summary: In particle physics, discrepancies between experimental measurements and Standard Model (SM) predictions are commonly interpreted within new theoretical models. In this context, the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) provides a general framework encompassing a broad class of models. However, exploring the enormous space of possible SMEFT operators rapidly becomes a challenging combinatorial problem: many operators can contribute simultaneously to different observables, their effects are correlated, and distinct operator combinations can provide comparably good descriptions of the data. In this work, we formulate the exploration of the SMEFT operator space as a sequential decision-making problem using reinforcement learning (RL). Our RL agent employs a lightweight actor-critic architecture with approximately 40K trainable parameters in total. Rather than searching for a single best-fit theory, our method is designed to discover a diverse set of high-quality theory hypotheses. We test the method in a complex phenomenological environment comprising 132 observables across several sectors of particle physics, including 24 measurements that deviate from their SM predictions by more than $1.5σ$. We show that the learned RL policy efficiently constructs multi-operator theories that substantially improve the global fit. Comparisons with independent random-subset and random-sequential searches demonstrate the ability of the RL policy to navigate this large combinatorial space. Our results establish RL as a systematic framework for exploring diverse patterns of new physics (NP) interactions within SMEFT.

papers.title: Heavy double-gluon quarkonium and $\overline{b}ggc$ mesons
papers.summary: We investigate heavy double-gluon hybrid mesons, built from a heavy quark-antiquark pair and two valence gluons, using the two-point QCD sum rule method. The charmonium-like $\bar{c}GGc$ and bottomonium-like $\bar{b}GGb$ states are considered with $J^{PC}=0^{\pm\pm}$ and $1^{\pm\pm}$, whereas the open-flavor $\bar{b}GGc$ states are classified by $J^{P}=0^{\pm}$ and $1^{\pm}$. The currents with $J^{PC}=0^{+-}, 0^{--}, 1^{++}$, and $1^{-+}$ vanish identically, so sum rules are derived for the remaining four channels. The operator product expansion is carried out up to dimension twelve, and the Borel parameter and continuum threshold are fixed so that the pole contribution dominates and the OPE converges. The resulting masses lie in the ranges $M\simeq 6.2$--$6.7$~GeV for $\bar{c}GGc$, $M\simeq 12.0$--$12.2$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGb$, and $M\simeq 9.2$--$9.6$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGc$, and the current couplings are obtained for all channels. These predictions provide a basis for analyzing the strong decays of double-gluon hybrids and for interpreting future experimental data in the heavy-quark sector.

papers.title: Inclusive Heavy Quarkonium Production in Lepton-Hadron Scattering in a Joint QCD+QED Factorization Approach
papers.summary: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will provide an opportunity for precision studies of heavy quarkonium production in electron-proton ($ep$) and electron-nucleus ($eA$) collisions. Comparing production in $ep$ and $eA$ collisions provides a clean, well-controlled experimental environment to study interactions between a heavy quark pair and nuclear matter and the formation of quarkonia in a nuclear medium. In this talk, we present the first calculation of heavy quarkonium production in both $ep$ and $eA$ collisions at EIC energies using a joint QCD+QED factorization framework that treats collision-induced QCD and QED radiation on equal footing, and discuss the role of the nuclear medium in exploring how a physical quarkonium is emerged from a produced heavy quark pair. We also systematically extend our calculation to include next-to-leading power contributions in the inverse power expansion of quarkonium transverse momentum, and discuss the matching of our calculations to fixed-order calculations in the nonrelativistic Quantum Chromodynamics (NRQCD) approach.
papers.comments: 5 pages, 2 figures; contributed talk to HardProbes2026

papers.title: Generating a simple silicon detector simulation with an open-weight large language model
papers.summary: Recent LLM developments have seen AI-generated code become commonplace in the software development industry. Without tool access, LLMs cannot execute simulations, and their knowledge of toolkits such as Geant4 is limited. We demonstrate here, a detector simulation workflow with a Qwen3.6-27B model with Q4_K_M GGUF quantisation together with custom resources and tools served via MCP servers to generate a particle detector simulation. In 50 independent runs, 42(29--56)% at 95% CI produced energy-deposit distributions statistically consistent with a reference simulation, measured against a reference simulation. These results provide a proof of concept that MC simulations can be generated using text-based prompts with an LLM, given the necessary resources and tools. More extensive resources, such as example code and additional documentation, are likely to be required for more complex simulation tasks.

papers.title: Third-body-corrected Two-Pion Femtoscopic Correlations in Au+Au Collisions at High Baryon Density
papers.summary: Identical charged pion femtoscopy provides a sensitive probe of the space-time structure of particle-emitting sources in heavy-ion collisions. At high baryon density, the differences between $π^+π^+$ and $π^-π^-$ Hanbury Brown--Twiss (HBT) radii may originate from both the third-body Coulomb effect and the initial-state isospin asymmetry. Since the latter is related to the equation of state (EoS) of asymmetric nuclear matter, separating these two effects is essential. In these proceedings, we present the measurements of identical charged pion correlations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=3.0$, 3.2, 3.5, 3.9, 4.5, and 7.7 GeV collected by the STAR experiment. A correction procedure is developed to remove the residual third-body Coulomb effect. After correction, the extracted HBT radii of $π^+π^+$ and $π^-π^-$ become consistent within uncertainties. The results indicate that the observed charge dependence is dominated by the third-body Coulomb effect, while any remaining contribution from the initial-state isospin asymmetry to the relative HBT radius difference, $(R_{π^-}-R_{π^+})/R_{π^+}$, is constrained to be less than 5\% at the 95\% confidence level.

papers.title: Evaluation of Performance of the p-stop fabrication process variations in ATLAS18 strip sensors, Pre- and Post-Irradiation
papers.summary: The High-Luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) requires the replacement of the ATLAS Inner Detector with a new all-silicon Inner Tracker (ITk). Radiation-hard n-in-p micro-strip sensors were developed for use in the ITk. During quality control (QC) and quality assurance (QA) procedures performed on ATLAS18 production sensors and test chips, ATLAS ITk strip sensor institutes identified instances of low p-stop density in certain production batches. To investigate the origin of these issues and to try some technological improvements, two dedicated sample batches with four variations of the p-stop fabrication process were produced. These process types (1-4) were systematically evaluated to determine their effectiveness and uniformity. In total, 56 full-size sensors, along with numerous miniature sensors and test chips, were tested. A number of samples were used in the irradiation campaign reaching the maximum expected levels for the HL-LHC operation after 10 years - with neutrons up to 1.6E15 neq/cm2, and with gamma rays from a 60Co source up to 66 Mrad. The goal of this evaluation program is to assess the impact of of p-stop fabrication process variations on interstrip isolation performance and to provide feedback for future sensor development. This paper describes the applied test procedures and presents the corresponding results, which demonstrate good sensor performance for all investigated p-stop types. The findings confirm the reliability of the evaluated designs and identify specific advantages that can inform further optimization of strip sensor fabrication.

papers.title: Hunting dark matter: the present and future of direct particle detection
papers.summary: The nature of dark matter remains one of the major open questions in particle physics and cosmology. Direct detection experiments aim to identify dark matter particles through their interactions with ordinary matter, but despite substantial improvements in experimental sensitivity, no conclusive detection has been achieved. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the present status and future prospects of direct particle detection, focusing on searches for dark matter particles from the Galactic halo. We introduce the theoretical framework for interpreting experimental results, including nuclear and electron scattering, collective excitations, particle absorption, and time- and direction-dependent signatures. We review the detection technologies employed in these searches, highlighting their operating principles, advantages, and limitations, as well as the calibration techniques and background mitigation strategies required to achieve high sensitivity. Particular emphasis is placed on experimental results reported since 2020, covering nuclear and electron recoil searches, annual modulation measurements, and directional detection. We also discuss experiments under construction and proposed future detectors, ranging from large-scale noble-liquid experiments to low-threshold technologies targeting sub-GeV dark matter. Finally, we examine the challenges that will shape the next generation of experiments, including the need for increasingly low energy thresholds, improved background understanding and discrimination, and the growing importance of neutrino-induced backgrounds. The diversity and complementarity of detector technologies will remain essential for exploring the dark matter parameter space and establishing the nature of any potential signal.

papers.title: Particle Identification Studies using a Highly Granular Crystal Electromagnetic Calorimeter
papers.summary: A proposal for the Circular Electron Positron Collider electromagnetic calorimeter is a highly granular scintillating crystal design that uses silicon photomultipliers to measure physics signals from photons. The potential to develop particle identification methods using deep and traditional machine learning is explored. A contrastive machine learning technique was found to enable the separation of showering and 'punch-through' pions without explicit labels. A supervised particle identification method was then trained using the results, using both a graph neural network and a boosted decision tree to distinguish electron, showering hadron, and minimum-ionizing-particle-like events. The classifier achieved an area-under-the-receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.996 for both cases. A Shapley additive explanations analysis showed the boosted decision tree classifier matched expectations for each event type. The particle identification capability is then demonstrated on experimental data taken from the CERN Proton Synchrotron T9 beamline.

papers.title: Inferring the neutral-current neutrino--nucleon cross section from IceCube data
papers.summary: Neutrinos interact only via the weak force, through the exchange of $W^{\pm}$ and $Z^{0}$ bosons in charged-current and neutral-current interactions, respectively. Recent experiments have measured the charged-current cross section at high energies, whereas neutral-current interactions remain largely unexplored experimentally. In this work, we investigate the sensitivity of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory to the neutral-current neutrino--nucleon cross section using 12 years of data. We consider two strategies to constrain this quantity: $(i)$ leveraging neutrino absorption and regeneration as neutrinos traverse the Earth; and $(ii)$ using the track-to-cascade event ratio. We find that current IceCube data can set only an upper limit on the neutral-current neutrino--nucleon cross section. We further show that IceCube-Gen2 should be able to constrain the neutral-current cross section with both methods considered here.

papers.title: Muon and Tau Anomalies and $Δα_{had}^{(5)} (M_Z^2)$ in the Standard Model
papers.summary: I review the present status of the Standard Model (SM) determination of the muon anomaly by emphasizing the estimate of the lowest hadronic vacuum polarization contributions using recent $e^+e^-$ data on $2π$ and $3π$ and the inclusive ratio $R^{ee}$ of total cross-sections compiled by PDG to which we add the QCD continuum including HO PT QCD up to $α_s^5$, quark mass $m_q^2$ up to $α_s^3$, $m_s^4$ up to $α_s^2$ and QCD condensates. Adding the $e^+e^-\to π^0γ+ ηγ$ contributions to the CMD3 data, one obtains\,: $a_μ\vert^{hvp}_{lo}=(7094\pm 37)\times 10^{-11}$. Combining this LO result with the HO estimate of the hadronic, QED and EW contributions, one obtains\,: $Δa_μ^{sm} \equiv (a_μ^{exp}-a_μ^{sm})= (86\pm 38_{th}\pm 14.5_{exp})\times 10^{-11} $. The average of the recent estimates quoted in Table\,3 [$\oplus$ attempt to fit all $\,e^+e^-$ data] gives\,: $Δa_μ^{sm} = (84.9[90.0]\pm 21.3_{th}\pm 14.5_{exp})\times 10^{-11}$\,. These results agree with the precise BMW20 lattice one and still suggest a window for new physics beyond the SM of $(2.1\sim 3.5)\,σ$. Besides some future projects for improving the $e^+e^-$ data, the MUonE for extracting directly $a_μ^{tot}\vert^{hvp}_{lo}$ and J-PARC (E34) for an independent measurement of $a_μ$, it is important to improve the Lattice results shown in Fig.\,9 which (at first sight) disagree each others despite the large errors and may question the reliability of the {\it averages of different averages} used in the White Paper (WP25) Our analysis is completed by updating the estimate of the hadronic contribution to the tau anomaly\,: $a_τ\vert^{hvp}_{lo}=(3516\pm 25)\times 10^{-9}$ and to $α(M_Z)\,: \,Δα_{had}^{(5)} (M_Z^2)= (2770.7\pm 4.5)\times 10^{-5}. $
papers.comments: Latex sources, 19 pages, 3 Tables, 12 figures. Review talk given at QCD26(20-24 july 2026, Montpellier-FR) and at HEPMAD26 (26-31 october 2026, Antananarivo-MG)

papers.title: Directionality of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO experiment
papers.summary: Electron-recoil directionality can help distinguish solar-neutrino interactions from backgrounds and, together with recoil-energy measurements and three-dimensional tracking, enable neutrino-energy spectroscopy. We study the reconstruction of the initial direction of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO optical time-projection chamber, focusing on the 50 L LIME prototype and its high-granularity scientific CMOS (sCMOS) readout. A dedicated algorithm identifies the interaction point from the asymmetry of the track light distribution and estimates the recoil direction from the early portion of the ionization trail, before multiple scattering erases most of the directional information. The method is characterized with a detailed Monte Carlo simulation of electron recoils and detector response. Samples spanning 15 keV to 70 keV are used to optimize the algorithm parameters by minimizing the width of the reconstructed-minus-true projected-angle distribution. The projected angular response is modeled by two Gaussian components that account for its dependence on track inclination. The narrower component, associated with favorable projections approximately parallel to the Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) plane, has a width that improves from about $20^\circ$ near 20 keV to about $12^\circ$ at 60 keV. We also quantify the fraction of events in the correctly reconstructed angular core and discuss the dominant limitations of a camera-only two-dimensional measurement.
papers.comments: 17 pages, 9 figures, 1 table. Prepared for submission to JCAP

papers.title: Dimension-seven spectator effects in charm-hadron lifetimes at NLO
papers.summary: We compute the next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections to the connected current-current part of the dimension-seven spectator coefficients in the heavy-quark expansion of charm-hadron widths. The finite terms are fixed in NDR-$\overline{\rm MS}$, with the evanescent operators defined by the standard Greek projection and averaged over Hermitian-conjugate pairs, and with a finite subtraction that sets the finite mixing of the dimension-seven operators into the dimension-six ones to zero. In several channels the one-loop term is comparable to the LO coefficient, and two operator families absent at LO are generated. Since the NLO matrix elements of the dimension-seven operators are not known, we estimate the effect of the coefficients on the widths with tree-level matrix elements from vacuum insertion for $D$ mesons and from the bag model for charmed baryons. The $1/m_c$ corrections to the matrix elements of the dimension-six QCD operators are treated by a naive expansion. Without their $O(α_s)$ part the semileptonic width of the $D_s^+$ would be negative. The NLO dimension-seven correction raises the $D^+$ width by 0.78 ps$^{-1}$, so that its central value, slightly negative as published, becomes positive. At central inputs, it is about 1% of the $D^0$ width, 10% of the $D_s^+$ width and at most 2% of the widths of the singly charmed baryons. Added to the published pole-scheme width, the $D^+$ correction gives $τ(D^+)=1.41^{+\infty}_{-0.76}$ ps. The NLO term reduces the scale dependence of the nonleptonic dimension-seven contribution severalfold for the singly charmed baryons, whose matrix elements are evolved, but not uniformly for the $D$ mesons.
papers.comments: 41 pages, 8 figures, 8 tables; Wilson coefficients and diagram-by-diagram code as ancillary files

papers.title: Doubly strange tetraquark as a $KK^*$ virtual state: quark-model study with harmonic traps
papers.summary: We extract hadron--hadron scattering information from quark-level interactions using an artificial harmonic trap and a four-quark basis that includes both meson--meson and compact diquark--antidiquark configurations. Combining the Busch--Englert--Rzażewski--Wilkens formula with the effective range expansion (ERE), we determine phase shifts, scattering lengths, effective ranges, and pole positions from the trapped spectrum. We control uncertainties from basis truncation, finite trap frequencies, truncation of ERE, and quark-model parameters. The extracted $DD^*$ and $BB^*$ binding energies agree with direct calculations, providing benchmarks. For the doubly strange $T_{ss}$ with $I(J^P)=0(1^+)$, we predict a $KK^*$ virtual-state pole about 30--35~MeV below threshold in the stable-$K^*$ approximation. Both the AL1 model and its modified version that better reproduces the measured $T_{cc}^+$ binding energy yield this result. This finding differs from earlier predictions of a bound state and motivates searches for the $T_{ss}$ at facilities such as the High Intensity heavy Ion Accelerator Facility (HIAF). This framework could be extended to other hadron-hadron channels to extract scattering observables and pole positions.

papers.title: First observation of the decay $D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{*+}γ$ and measurement of the branching-fraction ratio $\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{*+} γ]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{+} γ]$
papers.summary: We report the first observation of the radiative decay $D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{*+} γ$ with a significance greater than 10 standard deviations. The signal is found in $e^{+}e^{-} \to c\bar{c}$ production using data samples with integrated luminosities of 980 and 572~$\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ collected by the Belle and Belle~II detectors operating at the KEKB and SuperKEKB asymmetric-energy $e^{+}e^{-}$ colliders, respectively. The branching-fraction ratio $\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{*+} γ]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+} \to D_{s}^{+} γ]$ is measured to be $0.74 \pm 0.05 ({\rm stat.}) \pm 0.06 ({\rm syst.)}$. This result helps discriminate between different theoretical models regarding the internal structure of the charm-strange meson $D_{s1}(2460)^{+}$.

papers.title: A Paired Monte Carlo Intensity-Ratio Method for Incorporating Detector Resolution in Amplitude Analysis
papers.summary: Finite detector resolution can bias resonance parameters and fit fractions extracted from amplitude analyses. We present the paired Monte Carlo intensity-ratio method for incorporating resolution effects into amplitude analysis. The method uses ratios of reference intensities evaluated at paired truth-level and reconstructed kinematics to reweight the Monte Carlo normalization and approximately account for detector resolution. A resampling study of simulated $D^+\to K^+π^+π^-π^0$ decays shows that the method substantially reduces resolution-induced shifts in fitted resonance widths. Likelihood evaluation uses intensity calculations and normalization sums, avoiding a response convolution at each data event.

papers.title: Strong Decays of the $2^-$ Heavy-Light Mesons in the Relativistic Bethe-Salpeter Approach
papers.summary: We present a relativistic study of the mass spectra, the $^1D_2$--$^3D_2$ mixing angles, and the OZI-allowed two-body strong decays of the heavy-light $J^P=2^-$ mesons $D_2$, $D'_2$, $D_{s2}$, $D'_{s2}$, $\bar{B}_2$, $\bar{B}'_2$, $\bar{B}_{s2}$, and $\bar{B}'_{s2}$. The mass spectrum and the meson wave functions are obtained by solving the full instantaneous Bethe--Salpeter (Salpeter) equation, in which the wave-function representations are constructed directly in terms of the $J^P$ quantum numbers rather than the non-relativistic spectroscopic notation ${}^{2S+1}L_J$. For the decay amplitudes we use the partial conservation of the axial-vector current (PCAC) together with the low-energy theorem for the $H\to H'P$ channels, so that the light pseudoscalar meson enters only through its decay constant, and the effective chiral Lagrangian for the $H\to H'V$ channels. The total widths of these mesons are estimated by summing over the partial widths of all OZI-allowed strong decay channels.

papers.title: Fundamental physics with quantum sensors in space
papers.summary: Quantum sensors such as atomic clocks, atom interferometers, and atomic magnetometers can be used as sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model. Space offers microgravity, long baselines, low environmental noise, access to varying gravitational potentials, and unique opportunities involving the Sun, Moon, planets, and asteroids. These proceedings of the Aspen Center for Physics workshop on "Fundamental physics in space with quantum sensors," held February 22-27, 2026, summarize the scientific case, current capabilities, and space mission concepts for investigating dark matter, testing general relativity, and detecting gravitational waves in frequency bands inaccessible from the ground.

papers.title: A Forecast for Testing the Decreasing $H_0$ Trend in Time-Delay Cosmography
papers.summary: In 2019 the H0LiCOW/TDCOSMO collaboration reported a decreasing Hubble constant $H_0$ trend with lens redshift in the flat $Λ$CDM model at low statistical significance ($< 2 σ$). The signal is expected if physics is missing from the $Λ$CDM model in the late universe. In the wake of recent TDCOSMO 2026 results, we revisit the feature. Although the statistical significance of the trend has increased in a like-for-like comparison with earlier studies, propagating mass-sheet transformation (MST) uncertainties reduces the significance to $\sim 1 σ$. As a result, Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) currently favours a constant $H_0$ over a decreasing $H_0$ in the ratio 2.4:1. Nevertheless, we highlight good agreement on a negative slope with independent observables and forecast that approximately 40 and 90 lenses will be required to substantiate the trend at $\sim 2 σ$ and $\sim 3 σ$ significance, respectively, if the feature is physical and current uncertainties are representative. Even now, it is evident that the TDCOSMO 2026 $H_0$ constraint $H_0 \approx 71$ km/s/Mpc reflects an average over the lens redshift distribution and is naturally anchored at intermediate lens redshifts.

papers.title: Probing scalar-mediated Lorentz violation with hydrogen masers and spin-precession of molecules
papers.summary: We propose using hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession experiments, traditionally employed in precision frequency measurements and searches for the electron electric dipole moment, as complementary probes of light scalar-mediated, spin-dependent fifth forces. We investigate their sensitivity to Lorentz-violating interactions mediated by scalars with masses ranging from $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4}~μ\mathrm{eV})$ to $\mathcal{O}(10~\mathrm{keV})$. While hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession measurements probe different combinations of Lorentz-violating couplings, we find that the strongest projected sensitivities can be achieved using spin-precession of ultracold molecules, benefiting from their extended coherence times. These experimental approaches provide access to previously unexplored regions of parameter space, probing interaction ranges extending from centimeter to sub-angstrom scales. Our proposals highlight the potential of precision atomic and molecular experiments to search for new spin-dependent scalar-mediated interactions and violations of fundamental spacetime symmetries.
papers.comments: 43 pages, 10 figures, and 3 pages of appendices; comments are welcome

papers.title: On the Structure of the Nuclear-Clock Isotope $^{229}$Th Beyond Quadratic Order
papers.summary: Precision measurements of the exceptionally low-energy nuclear transition of $^{229}$Th, offer an extraordinary sensitivity to a variety of new light fields. However, interpreting such measurements requires nuclear-structure information beyond what is currently constrained by spectroscopy. We develop a systematic description of the electric multipole interactions governing the hyperfine structure of ${}^{229}$Th, including the hexadecapole contribution, and perform a symmetry-based analysis of the resulting hyperfine splittings in crystalline environments. Hyperfine spectroscopy generally constrains combinations of nuclear moments and crystal-field gradients, leading to degeneracies when higher multipole interactions are allowed. We then combine experimental nuclear observables, particle-rotor relations, and a deformed-Fermi charge-density model to investigate the electromagnetic contribution to the nuclear clock's sensitivity to variations in the fine-structure constant. We find that higher-order nuclear deformation and state-dependent differences in the radial charge distribution of the clock states can substantially alter the predicted sensitivity, introducing large uncertainties that are not constrained by existing measurements. Our results highlight the importance of combining nuclear and solid-state theory with complementary measurements, including spectroscopy of higher-spin states, to constrain the nuclear structure and improve predictions of the clock's sensitivity to new physics. Our symmetry-based analysis also provides a framework for using hyperfine spectroscopy to investigate local defect symmetries in crystalline hosts.

papers.title: $B\to K a$ decays in QCD factorization and revised bounds on ALP couplings
papers.summary: Rare flavor-changing processes such as $B\to K a$ offer sensitive probes of axion-like particles (ALPs) for masses below a few GeV. We study this process in the framework of QCD factorization and ALP effective theory, in which the ALP couples to the Standard Model (SM) fermions through shift-invariant derivative interactions. In contrast to previous studies, where flavor violation arises solely from flavor-changing ALP couplings, we also include the contributions proportional to flavor-conserving ALP couplings, in which the flavor change is mediated by the weak interactions of the SM. Based on this analysis, we derive upper bounds on both flavor-changing and flavor-conserving ALP couplings at low energies. Then we consider the UV scenario of a "minimally flavor-violating ALP", which features flavor-universal ALP-fermion couplings at very high energies, and evaluate the resulting constraints on the UV couplings.

papers.title: A new angle on coherence-violating logarithms in color-singlet processes
papers.summary: We introduce a new formulation for the resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the transverse energy flow in rapidity gaps in the Drell-Yan process. Our formalism allows us to resum coherence-violating logarithms in the gap cross section in the phenomenologically important regime where the gap size is comparable to the logarithm of the transverse energy. In the formal small gap limit, our result reduces to the known state-of-the-art resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the Drell-Yan process. However, we identify sizable new corrections even for moderate gap widths that significantly modify the phenomenological picture for LHC applications. This work will form an important element of future extensions to a range of global and non-global observables.

papers.title: Analytic next-to-leading order electroweak corrections to Higgs boson pair production in the forward limit
papers.summary: We calculate next-to-leading order electroweak corrections for Higgs boson pair production in the gluon fusion channel, in the forward limit. We perform an analytic calculation and obtain a final result for the partonic cross section that depends explicitly on all kinematic parameters and particle masses. We describe our method, which can be readily applied to similar processes. We observe rapid convergence within the validity range of the forward expansion. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the entire phase space can be covered when this approach is combined with the high-energy expansion.

papers.title: Mapping the multimessenger horizon for $γ$-ray counterparts of cosmic neutrinos
papers.summary: The joint detection of high-energy neutrinos and $γ$-rays offers a powerful probe of the most energetic astrophysical accelerators, linking hadronic interactions to observable signatures across cosmic distances. Understanding the conditions under which these two messengers can be simultaneously observed is essential for identifying and characterizing the sources of cosmic neutrinos. In this work, we examine the detectability of $γ$-ray cascades associated with neutrino production in source environments that are gamma-ray transparent, focusing on how electromagnetic cascades evolve as $γ$-rays propagate through intergalactic space. By modeling photon interactions with the extragalactic background light and deflections in intergalactic magnetic fields, we determine the minimum neutrino fluence for transient emission and neutrino flux for steady emission required to produce a $γ$-ray counterpart detectable by $γ$-ray observatories, such as Fermi-LAT, HAWC, or LHAASO. This defines a ``multimessenger horizon" -- the region in flux-distance parameter space where neutrinos and $γ$-rays are jointly observable. We consider both energy-binned injection tied to IceCube's sensitivity and a continuous power-law spectrum extending from TeV to PeV energies. Our results reveal that detectability depends strongly on redshift, magnetic field strength, and photon energy, with higher-energy cascades suffering greater attenuation inside filamentary structures. The framework provides new constraints on source opacity, baryon loading, and neutrino production mechanisms, offering a predictive tool for interpreting current events and guiding future multimessenger campaigns.

papers.title: Perturbative QCD Analysis for the Electric Dipole Moment of $Ξ$ and $Σ$ Hyperons from CP-Violating Dipole Interactions
papers.summary: Hyperon electric dipole moments (EDMs) probe CP-violating interactions beyond the Standard Model. Motivated by the recent BESIII measurement [Ablikim et al., Science 393, 1027] and the perturbative QCD analysis of the $Λ$ EDM form factor $d_Λ$ [Chen et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 051902], we extend the perturbative QCD calculation of the EDM form factor to the $Ξ$ and $Σ$ hyperons. We derive factorization formulas from quark EDM and chromoelectric dipole moment contributions in terms of leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs). Using lattice-QCD results for the LCDAs and the strange-quark dipole moment ranges inferred from the BESIII $d_Λ$ bound and neutron EDM constraints, we obtain the conditional estimates $-4.8 \times 10^{-18} < d_{Ξ^-} < 1.8\times10^{-18}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $-6.1\times10^{-19} < d_{Σ^+} < 2.4\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ at the scale of ${J/ψ}$ mass. Dedicated searches at BESIII and the future Super Tau-Charm Factory could further constrain these quark-level sources of CP violation.

papers.title: Smuggling baryon asymmetry through strong washout
papers.summary: We propose a scheme in which a primordial net baryon number generated at or around the unification scale may survive subsequent strong washout phases associated with active sphalerons and interactions of right-handed neutrinos inherent to thermal leptogenesis. A simple realization of this, namely, a long-lived scalar population injecting the net $B-L$ it carries into the Standard Model matter sector late enough to be safe from a strong washout, is constructed and studied in the context of a simple Pati-Salam scalar sector with a heavy $SU(4)_C$ sextet scalar.

papers.title: Active Galactic Nuclei as Beyond the Standard Model Laboratories: a White Paper
papers.summary: Multi-messenger and multi-wavelength observations of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) can provide otherwise inaccessible knowledge about physics Beyond the Standard Model (BSM), and may even lead to its discovery. Realizing this potential hinges on two parallel efforts: advancing our understanding of AGN and of the dark matter around them, and identifying the BSM signatures that are at once promising and robust against the gaps in that understanding. These fields have attracted growing interest in recent years, also motivated by the IceCube association of neutrinos to individual AGN, yet we have only begun to explore their cross-fertilization. This white paper offers a new perspective on this interdisciplinary endeavor. It concisely reviews the state of the art in each field and at their interface, and identifies the key open questions that must be addressed to strengthen our prospects for learning about BSM physics with AGN.

papers.title: Thermal Composite Dark Matter at LZ
papers.summary: We show that stable fermionic resonances of Composite Higgs models provide a thermal inelastic Dark Matter interpretation of the high-energy nuclear-recoil event LZ230616. Their stability follows from an exact accidental parity of the strong sector. Annihilation channels from composite interactions link the thermal relic mass to the strong coupling, allowing masses well beyond the pure electroweak prediction. We identify three scenarios in which the neutral states form a split pseudo-Dirac pair, distinguished by the origin of the inelastic coupling to the $Z$ boson. In the pure electroweak regime, the pair consists of the neutral components of a complex Higgsino-like doublet. Its unsuppressed inelastic $Z$ coupling requires Dark Matter masses above 20 TeV. In the pure strong regime, the suppressed $Z$ coupling of neutral states with vanishing hypercharge arises from strong interactions alone, allowing for smaller splittings and TeV-scale masses. In the third regime, which interpolates between the previous two, the neutral components of multiplets with different hypercharge are mixed. This enhances their inelastic coupling, accommodating the LZ event for masses of a few TeV and splittings around 300 keV, with mixing angles of order $10^\circ$. All three cases provide a thermal Dark Matter candidate able to explain the LZ event, consistently with the solar-capture bounds, the LZ high-energy sideband, and gamma-ray indirect searches.

papers.title: Plugging the Pion Chimney
papers.summary: Heavy QCD axions and other gluon-coupled axion-like particles (ALPs) with masses from MeV to GeV are well motivated and have been searched for extensively. However, a window around the neutral pion mass, the so-called pion chimney, has escaped every search. There the ALP mixes strongly with the $π^0$ and therefore shares its experimental signatures. We show that the chimney can be closed with existing LHC data. The key point is that mixing changes the lifetimes of the two mass eigenstates but does not make them equal, and at LHC energies the states are boosted enough for the lifetime to decide whether they escape the detector or decay inside it. The ATLAS monojet search constrains the first case and the ATLAS inclusive photon measurement the second, and together they exclude the chimney up to the cutoff of the ALP effective theory. Above the cutoff, LHC searches for the colored states of the simplest ultraviolet completions exclude the rest. We also show that the bound from the $K^+$ width does not reach the chimney, because an ALP passes the same selection as a $π^0$, and we derive an independent, purely kinematic constraint from the measured $π^\pm$-$π^0$ mass splitting.

papers.title: Supernova Bounds on Neutrino Dipole Moments from a Modern Perspective
papers.summary: Neutrinos may have nonstandard magnetic dipole moments $μ_ν$. In the dense cores of supernovae (SNe), these would convert part of the neutrinos into sterile, right-handed states through the electromagnetic fluctuations of the charged plasma. The streaming sterile neutrinos with 100-MeV energies can convert back to standard neutrinos in the Galactic magnetic field, leading to a high-energy neutrino flux unobserved from the historical SN 1987A. We reassess the production rates, including scattering on both protons and electrons, and, building upon advances in SN simulations and in the description of the Milky Way magnetic field, we revisit the bounds on magnetic dipole moments. We find for Dirac electron neutrinos $μ_{ν_e} \lesssim 4.8 \times 10^{-13} μ_B$, superseding all existing terrestrial and astrophysical constraints.

papers.title: Feebly-Interacting Particle Searches
papers.summary: In the last several years, feebly-interacting particles (FIPs) have moved from "exotica" to the mainstream of particle physics. This development is fueled by three motivations: FIPs are one of two broad possibilities for new particles, FIPs are as well motivated by dark matter as WIMPs, and FIPs are connected to important problems in particle physics. I review these motivations and then briefly highlight recent progress in a few areas, including axion-like particles, dark photons and other gauge bosons, the X17 anomaly, quirks, and the Forward Physics Facility.
papers.comments: 10 pages, to appear in the Proceedings of ICHEP 2026, the 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics, Natal, Brazil, 30 July to 5 August 2026

papers.title: 21 cm Cosmology of Boosted Dark Matter
papers.summary: The formation history of low-mass halos is sensitive to the properties of dark matter. At low redshift, nonlinear evolution and baryonic processes can obscure this information. The 21 cm signal provides access to a high-redshift stage of structure formation, when the abundance and clustering of low-mass halos retain direct sensitivity to the mass and interactions of dark matter. Boosted dark matter (BDM) realizes this possibility through a two-component scenario in which the annihilation of the heavier component converts part of the mass difference into kinetic energy of the lighter component. Self-interactions redistribute this energy and generate pressure support, suppressing small-scale density perturbations even for dark matter masses in the MeV range. We calculate the global 21 cm brightness temperature and its power spectrum in BDM cosmology. The reduced abundance of low-mass halos delays the global absorption feature and shifts the characteristic redshift evolution of the power spectrum. We assess the projected sensitivity of SKA1-Low to these signatures. The sensitivity is strongest at intermediate light-component fractions, where both components remain sufficiently abundant for self-heating to affect structure formation. For $σ_{\rm self1}/m_1\simeq0.1\,{\rm cm^2\,g^{-1}}$, models with $0.2\lesssim r_1\lesssim0.7$ can be distinguished from the fiducial $Λ$CDM prediction at the $95\%$ confidence level under the optimistic forecast. We compare our results with existing direct-detection bounds from SENSEI and prospects for BDM searches at large-volume neutrino experiments, including Super-/Hyper-Kamiokande, JUNO, and DUNE. This comparison highlights the unique and complementary role of high-redshift surveys in testing BDM models.

papers.title: The SymTFT and Quantum Phases of Matter
papers.summary: The symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) provides a unified framework for ordinary and generalized symmetries of quantum many-body systems. By encoding symmetry in a topological theory in one higher dimension, it separates symmetry data from the details of a specific quantum system. In this review, we give a pedagogical introduction to this framework and survey its applications to phases of quantum matter. For fusion category symmetries in ${(1+1)}$d, we explain how the SymTFT characterizes anomalies, classifies gapped phases, and organizes the symmetry structure of gapless phases. We also give a broad overview of further developments of this framework, including extensions to symmetries in higher dimensions, continuous symmetries, fermionic systems, mixed states, and spacetime symmetries.
papers.comments: Review article, to appear in "Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics"

papers.title: The Skyrme-Dilaton and Nucleon Observables
papers.summary: We extend the Skyrme model by incorporating the $σ/f_0(500)$-meson as a dilaton. The motivation is twofold: the $σ$-meson is the lightest scalar resonance in QCD and is therefore the natural extensions to the pions of the classical Skyrme model, while its interpretation as a pseudo-Goldstone boson of spontaneously broken scale symmetry is supported by recent studies of gravitational form factors and related developments. Although the $σ$-meson is a broad resonance, for static observables it can be treated as real particle since its line-shape is not expected to be essential. A combined fit to static nucleon observables yields $χ^2/\mathrm{dof} $ close to unity, with substantial improvement over the original Skyrme model, while simultaneously reproducing the physical value of $F_π$, the overall scale of the model.

papers.title: A Reinforcement Learning Method to Navigate SMEFT Operator Space
papers.summary: In particle physics, discrepancies between experimental measurements and Standard Model (SM) predictions are commonly interpreted within new theoretical models. In this context, the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) provides a general framework encompassing a broad class of models. However, exploring the enormous space of possible SMEFT operators rapidly becomes a challenging combinatorial problem: many operators can contribute simultaneously to different observables, their effects are correlated, and distinct operator combinations can provide comparably good descriptions of the data. In this work, we formulate the exploration of the SMEFT operator space as a sequential decision-making problem using reinforcement learning (RL). Our RL agent employs a lightweight actor-critic architecture with approximately 40K trainable parameters in total. Rather than searching for a single best-fit theory, our method is designed to discover a diverse set of high-quality theory hypotheses. We test the method in a complex phenomenological environment comprising 132 observables across several sectors of particle physics, including 24 measurements that deviate from their SM predictions by more than $1.5σ$. We show that the learned RL policy efficiently constructs multi-operator theories that substantially improve the global fit. Comparisons with independent random-subset and random-sequential searches demonstrate the ability of the RL policy to navigate this large combinatorial space. Our results establish RL as a systematic framework for exploring diverse patterns of new physics (NP) interactions within SMEFT.

papers.title: Non-Canonical Q-balls in Polyattractor Inflation Models
papers.summary: We show that Q-balls can exist in supergravity-based polyattractor inflation models that interpolate between $α$-attractor T-models and polynomial attractor models. We consider both the original polyattractor potential and a natural generalisation. We find that Q-balls solutions exist when the model deviates significantly from the T-model $α$-attractor, whereas in the T-model limit no Q-balls exist. These are non-canonical Q-balls due to the non-canonical kinetic term of the complex inflaton field. Such Q-balls could have significant cosmological consequences if they are produced at the end of inflation. In particular, if the global $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry of the supergravity-based polyattractor model is unbroken, the Q-balls can be absolutely stable and could account for dark matter.

papers.title: Heavy double-gluon quarkonium and $\overline{b}ggc$ mesons
papers.summary: We investigate heavy double-gluon hybrid mesons, built from a heavy quark-antiquark pair and two valence gluons, using the two-point QCD sum rule method. The charmonium-like $\bar{c}GGc$ and bottomonium-like $\bar{b}GGb$ states are considered with $J^{PC}=0^{\pm\pm}$ and $1^{\pm\pm}$, whereas the open-flavor $\bar{b}GGc$ states are classified by $J^{P}=0^{\pm}$ and $1^{\pm}$. The currents with $J^{PC}=0^{+-}, 0^{--}, 1^{++}$, and $1^{-+}$ vanish identically, so sum rules are derived for the remaining four channels. The operator product expansion is carried out up to dimension twelve, and the Borel parameter and continuum threshold are fixed so that the pole contribution dominates and the OPE converges. The resulting masses lie in the ranges $M\simeq 6.2$--$6.7$~GeV for $\bar{c}GGc$, $M\simeq 12.0$--$12.2$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGb$, and $M\simeq 9.2$--$9.6$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGc$, and the current couplings are obtained for all channels. These predictions provide a basis for analyzing the strong decays of double-gluon hybrids and for interpreting future experimental data in the heavy-quark sector.

papers.title: Inclusive Heavy Quarkonium Production in Lepton-Hadron Scattering in a Joint QCD+QED Factorization Approach
papers.summary: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will provide an opportunity for precision studies of heavy quarkonium production in electron-proton ($ep$) and electron-nucleus ($eA$) collisions. Comparing production in $ep$ and $eA$ collisions provides a clean, well-controlled experimental environment to study interactions between a heavy quark pair and nuclear matter and the formation of quarkonia in a nuclear medium. In this talk, we present the first calculation of heavy quarkonium production in both $ep$ and $eA$ collisions at EIC energies using a joint QCD+QED factorization framework that treats collision-induced QCD and QED radiation on equal footing, and discuss the role of the nuclear medium in exploring how a physical quarkonium is emerged from a produced heavy quark pair. We also systematically extend our calculation to include next-to-leading power contributions in the inverse power expansion of quarkonium transverse momentum, and discuss the matching of our calculations to fixed-order calculations in the nonrelativistic Quantum Chromodynamics (NRQCD) approach.
papers.comments: 5 pages, 2 figures; contributed talk to HardProbes2026

papers.title: Generalized transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions of a photon and orbital angular momentum
papers.summary: The coefficients of generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) that encode the canonical fermion orbital angular momentum and spin--orbit correlation do not contribute to the direct transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) and generalized-parton-distribution (GPD) projections. We present, to our knowledge, the first explicit calculation of the leading-twist, time-even, chiral-even fermion GTMDs of an on-shell real photon at zero skewness and order $α$. The coefficients $\mathcal{F}_A$ and $\mathcal{G}_A$, which multiply the $k_\perp\timesΔ_\perp$ structure, yield the fermion orbital angular momentum $\ell_z^f$ and spin--orbit correlation $\mathcal{C}_z^f$. For photon helicity $+1$, both are obtained in closed form in the leading fermion--antifermion sector and obey $\mathcal{C}_z^f=-\ell_z^f/2$ for a common transverse regulator independent of $x$, because the channel with the active fermion's spin anti-aligned with its orbital motion carries three times the integrated weight of the aligned channel. The projections reproduce the known photon TMDs and leading-logarithmic photon-to-fermion kernels, and energy-momentum-tensor overlaps reproduce the known one-loop photon gravitational form factors $F_1$, $F_2$, and $F_3$. Our result provides an analytic benchmark for fermionic orbital and spin--orbit structure in the real photon.

papers.title: Pulsar Timing Correlations Induced by Stochastic Spin-2 Ultralight Dark Matter
papers.summary: Ultralight dark matter (ULDM) can generate time-dependent gravitational perturbations, providing a potential signal for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). In Galactic halos, the velocity dispersion of ULDM gives rise to finite spatial coherence, which influences the correlations between pulsar timing signals. In this work, we derive the timing-residual cross-correlations induced by rapid metric oscillations of spin-2 ULDM, allowing for general polarization statistics. Under equipartition among the five polarization modes, the intrinsic angular kernel contains monopole and quadrupole components and exhibits an angular profile closely resembling that of spin-1 ULDM, suggesting a potential degeneracy between the two ULDM candidates in PTA observations.

papers.title: Mono-Z Signatures of Vector Dark Matter Detection at Future Electron-Positron Colliders: FCC-ee and ILC
papers.summary: We investigate the mono-$Z$ signature of a vector dark matter (VDM) model at future electron-positron colliders. In this model, a stable vector boson, arising from an extended $U(1)$ gauge symmetry, serves as a viable DM candidate that interacts with the Standard Model (SM) through a Higgs portal. We perform a detailed cut-based analysis for the mono-$Z$ channel at the FCC-ee (with $\sqrt{s}=240$ and $365$ GeV) and the ILC (with $\sqrt{s}=1$ TeV), considering both leptonic and hadronic decays of the $Z$ boson. Signal significances are evaluated for benchmark points using fast event simulation with MadGraph5, PYTHIA8, and Delphes3. Our results demonstrate that future $e^+e^-$ colliders provide excellent sensitivity to Higgs-portal VDM, with the ILC's beam polarization offering an additional handle to suppress SM backgrounds. This study highlights the potential of lepton colliders in probing DM interactions.

papers.title: Soft momentum expansion about the Stokes topological limit of Bogoliubov coefficients
papers.summary: It is known that particle production in time-dependent cosmological backgrounds can be computed using the Stokes phenomena occurring in Bogoliubov transformations with an analytically continued time coordinate. We analytically compute the soft momentum expansion of the particle production amplitude about the Stokes topological limit that was recently discovered in this context. The computational technique relies on an exponentially improved asymptotic expansion that involves automorphisms in the space of functions defined partly by the angular step function intrinsic to the Stokes topological sectors. We combine this with special discrete symmetries tied to the time dependence of the dispersion relation $ω_k^2(z) = C(k) + A z^n$ for even $n$ to explicitly compute the leading momentum dependence of the amplitude which is nonperturbative in $A$. We also use this result to give a semi-analytic estimate of the number density of particles in this class of scenarios.

papers.title: Phenomenology of neutrino mass ordering synergies in reactor, accelerator, and atmospheric neutrino experiments, and the role of the detector response
papers.summary: The neutrino mass ordering is one of the main open questions of neutrino physics, addressed by reactor, accelerator, and atmospheric experiments and by their combination. When the data are fitted under the wrong ordering, each experiment returns its own value of $Δm^2_{31}$, its wrong-ordering solution. We show that this solution is a weighted average of the values preferred by the individual bins of the measured event spectra, in reconstructed energy and, for atmospheric neutrinos, also zenith angle, with weights set by their statistical precision. Both the values and the weights depend on the detector response. In the plane of $Δm^2_{31}$ fitted under the two orderings, the solutions lie on lines of slope close to $-1$, so that each experiment is described by one intercept. The weighted bin average extends the mass ordering sum rule to any oscillation experiment, including atmospheric neutrinos in Earth matter. It recovers the known closed forms for short-baseline reactors and for accelerators in vacuum, and for JUNO it equals a closed form evaluated at one effective energy, which depends on the energy resolution. Above the MSW resonance the frequency of atmospheric $ν_μ$ disappearance becomes nearly independent of $δ_{CP}$, and the $ν_μ$ disappearance solution moves mainly with $θ_{23}$. The atmospheric intercept depends on the energy and direction resolutions, the energy window, and the event classes, and differs between detectors. The synergy of two experiments is determined by the separation of their intercepts relative to their precisions on $|Δm^2_{31}|$. With JUNO, this separation depends strongly on $δ_{CP}$ for an accelerator and is nearly independent of $δ_{CP}$ and $θ_{23}$ for IceCube DeepCore using all channels.
papers.comments: 46 pages, 14 figures, 2 tables. Code available at https://github.com/vanessacerrone/nmo-synergies

papers.title: Heavy-quark gluon radiation in transversely flowing QCD matter: First-subeikonal corrections
papers.summary: We investigate medium-induced gluon radiation from energetic heavy quarks propagating through a finite-size QCD medium with transverse collective flow. Within the DGLV framework, we calculate the radiation spectrum at first order in opacity and to first-subeikonal accuracy, retaining finite heavy-quark and effective gluon masses. Subleading corrections to the longitudinal propagator poles generate mass-dependent modifications of both the residue denominators and formation phases. For rotationally symmetric transverse-momentum integration domains, all contributions linear in the transverse flow velocity vanish after full azimuthal integration, while a nonzero static first-subeikonal correction remains. For representative medium parameters, this correction increases the integrated fractional radiative energy loss by approximately $10$--$20\%$, depending on the quark mass, initial energy, and path length. At the differential level, transverse flow produces a dipolar angular anisotropy, enhancing radiation along the flow direction and suppressing it in the opposite direction.

papers.title: Suppression, flow, and chemical components of heavy flavor hadrons in relativistic heavy-ion collisions within an improved Langevin framework
papers.summary: We improve the Langevin model to incorporate both perturbative and non-perturbative interactions between heavy quarks and the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The transport coefficient of heavy quarks is evaluated by a potential scattering model in which both the short-range Yukawa interaction and the long-range string interaction are included. The updated model provides the correct thermal equilibrium limit of the heavy quark system with the medium background, and improves the accuracy in describing the nuclear modification factor and elliptic flow coefficient of $D$ mesons observed at RHIC and the LHC. Nuclear modification of different chemical components of charm hadrons, including $D^0$, $D_s^+$, $Λ_c^+$, $Ξ_c^0$, and $Ω_c^0$, is investigated. Their spectrum ratios are found sensitive to not only the hadronization mechanism of charm quarks but also the medium-modified charm quark spectrum in heavy-ion collisions, offering additional constraints on the heavy quark dynamics inside a color-deconfined nuclear medium.

papers.title: Thermal deep inelastic scattering, universality and complex geodesics
papers.summary: In deep inelastic scattering (DIS), a lepton scatters off a target hadron whose structure is probed by an exchanged photon with large spacelike virtuality. We consider two-point functions of currents in strongly interacting quantum field theories at finite temperature in this kinematic regime and use a holographic description to compute them. At large virtuality, the crossover from vacuum-dominated to thermally dominated physics corresponds to a transition from exponentially suppressed absorption to power-law behavior of the response functions. This regime is related to a particular near-lightcone limit of thermal CFT correlators. We show that the response functions exhibit a large degree of universality: the dependence on the three-point couplings of currents to the stress tensor enters through a channel-dependent coefficient multiplying the kinematic parameter that controls the relative size of vacuum and thermal effects. The same coefficient controls conformal collider bounds; when either bound is saturated, the corresponding response function takes its vacuum form in the near-lightcone limit. Furthermore, the absorption exponent in the low-temperature regime is related to a complex geodesic propagating in the near-lightcone geometry.

papers.title: Global analysis of the $ρ$ resonance in lattice QCD
papers.summary: We present a lattice-QCD study of the $ρ$ resonance in which we address the quark-mass and lattice-spacing dependence in a novel way using a global analysis of four $N_f=2+1$ ensembles. We parametrize discretization effects in the lattice energy levels and not in the scattering amplitude, which is defined in the continuum. We describe the amplitude using a $K$-matrix parameterization, which contains the light- and strange-quark mass dependence. By varying the parameterizations of quark-mass and lattice-spacing dependence, we examine the sensitivity of the physical-limit $ρ$ pole position to these choices and obtain the result $\sqrt{s}_ρ= 744(11)(7) - i\,69(7)(3)~\text{MeV}$ from a model average.

papers.title: Probing the QCD critical point through linearized sound wave dispersion and attenuation at finite baryon density
papers.summary: We investigate the linearized sound-channel response of a finite baryon density Israel-Stewart hydrodynamic system coupled to a parameterized equation of state containing a critical end point. The attenuation of sound is characterized by a threshold wavelength below which sound perturbations are strongly damped. We systematically study the dependence of this threshold scale on the non-universal parameters of the Beam Energy Scan Theory (BEST) equation of state framework. In our present study, the threshold wavelength remains finite but develops a pronounced peak in the vicinity of the critical end point, indicating strong absorption of sound modes on fireball-scale wavelengths. We further estimate the impact of this enhanced attenuation on the linearized anisotropic flow response and find a reduction of the elliptic and triangular flow harmonics near the critical region. Our results establish a phenomenological connection between critical sound attenuation, Mach cone like correlations, and the linearized flow response in baryon rich QCD matter. These results suggest a non-monotonic beam-energy dependence of the sound attenuation scale. Together with a corresponding suppression of Mach cone like correlations and the linearized anisotropic flow response, they may provide a consistent signature that the system trajectory passes close to the critical point of the chosen equation of state.

papers.title: A consistent (3D) EFT expansion of the bubble nucleation rate. Part I: scalar theories
papers.summary: Precise predictions of bubble nucleation are essential for connecting cosmological phase transitions to their potential observational signatures. In this first paper of a two-part series, we develop a general, fully perturbative framework for incorporating higher-dimensional operators (HDOs) into nucleation calculations in scalar high-temperature effective field theories. Our approach consistently includes their effects on the bounce and the fluctuations around it, including interactions with higher derivatives. We prove that the resulting statistical rate is invariant under field redefinitions, and establish sufficient conditions for the existence of the perturbative bounce solution in the presence of HDOs. We illustrate the framework by applying it to a model containing a scalar and a fermion, where we find modest HDO corrections in its regime of moderately strong transitions. We thus extend the systematic study of HDO effects beyond critical thermodynamics and provide a controlled method for determining their impact on bubble nucleation.

papers.title: Cosmological Collider Signals from Fermion Bubble Loops with a Chemical Potential
papers.summary: We present the first systematic analytical calculation of the local and nonlocal cosmological collider (CC) signals generated by massive fermion bubble loops in the presence of an effective chemical potential during inflation. Working in the de Sitter approximation, we investigate the four-point correlator of inflaton perturbations in the single-squeezed limit. By combining CC cutting rules, late-time expansions, and partial Mellin-Barnes (MB) techniques, we derive analytical expressions for both local and nonlocal signals. In particular, we identify two distinct contributions to the local signal, arising from spectrum and integer poles and from ultraviolet poles of the loop-momentum integral. We further investigate the three-point limit, where the separately extracted local and nonlocal contributions develop apparent folded singularities. By reorganizing the MB representation, we demonstrate that these singularities cancel in the complete signal and obtain a convergent double-MB integral suitable for numerical evaluation. Independent calculations using complementary MB representations provide nontrivial consistency checks of our results. We find that the chemical potential can significantly enhance the oscillatory signal while increasing its logarithmic oscillation frequency. Our analytical results provide a foundation for further studies of chemical-potential-enhanced fermionic CC signals, including fermion triangle loops.

papers.title: Inferring the neutral-current neutrino--nucleon cross section from IceCube data
papers.summary: Neutrinos interact only via the weak force, through the exchange of $W^{\pm}$ and $Z^{0}$ bosons in charged-current and neutral-current interactions, respectively. Recent experiments have measured the charged-current cross section at high energies, whereas neutral-current interactions remain largely unexplored experimentally. In this work, we investigate the sensitivity of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory to the neutral-current neutrino--nucleon cross section using 12 years of data. We consider two strategies to constrain this quantity: $(i)$ leveraging neutrino absorption and regeneration as neutrinos traverse the Earth; and $(ii)$ using the track-to-cascade event ratio. We find that current IceCube data can set only an upper limit on the neutral-current neutrino--nucleon cross section. We further show that IceCube-Gen2 should be able to constrain the neutral-current cross section with both methods considered here.

papers.title: Longitudinal Parton Correlations in MRW-Type Unintegrated Double Parton Distributions
papers.summary: Double parton scattering offers a way to investigate correlations between partons inside the proton that are absent from the usual product approximation for double parton distributions. In this contribution, we discuss how these correlations enter unintegrated double parton distributions when transverse momentum is generated using MRW-type prescriptions. Starting from non-factorized GS09 distributions evolved to unequal scales, we examine the double LO-MRW, virtuality-ordered MRW, and modified KMRW constructions, focusing on their transverse-momentum dependence and flavor structure.
papers.comments: 6 pages, contribution to the QCD at the Extremes 2026 proceedings. Summarizes results published in Eur. Phys. J. C 86 (2026) 1002; see arXiv:2605.15853

papers.title: Muon and Tau Anomalies and $Δα_{had}^{(5)} (M_Z^2)$ in the Standard Model
papers.summary: I review the present status of the Standard Model (SM) determination of the muon anomaly by emphasizing the estimate of the lowest hadronic vacuum polarization contributions using recent $e^+e^-$ data on $2π$ and $3π$ and the inclusive ratio $R^{ee}$ of total cross-sections compiled by PDG to which we add the QCD continuum including HO PT QCD up to $α_s^5$, quark mass $m_q^2$ up to $α_s^3$, $m_s^4$ up to $α_s^2$ and QCD condensates. Adding the $e^+e^-\to π^0γ+ ηγ$ contributions to the CMD3 data, one obtains\,: $a_μ\vert^{hvp}_{lo}=(7094\pm 37)\times 10^{-11}$. Combining this LO result with the HO estimate of the hadronic, QED and EW contributions, one obtains\,: $Δa_μ^{sm} \equiv (a_μ^{exp}-a_μ^{sm})= (86\pm 38_{th}\pm 14.5_{exp})\times 10^{-11} $. The average of the recent estimates quoted in Table\,3 [$\oplus$ attempt to fit all $\,e^+e^-$ data] gives\,: $Δa_μ^{sm} = (84.9[90.0]\pm 21.3_{th}\pm 14.5_{exp})\times 10^{-11}$\,. These results agree with the precise BMW20 lattice one and still suggest a window for new physics beyond the SM of $(2.1\sim 3.5)\,σ$. Besides some future projects for improving the $e^+e^-$ data, the MUonE for extracting directly $a_μ^{tot}\vert^{hvp}_{lo}$ and J-PARC (E34) for an independent measurement of $a_μ$, it is important to improve the Lattice results shown in Fig.\,9 which (at first sight) disagree each others despite the large errors and may question the reliability of the {\it averages of different averages} used in the White Paper (WP25) Our analysis is completed by updating the estimate of the hadronic contribution to the tau anomaly\,: $a_τ\vert^{hvp}_{lo}=(3516\pm 25)\times 10^{-9}$ and to $α(M_Z)\,: \,Δα_{had}^{(5)} (M_Z^2)= (2770.7\pm 4.5)\times 10^{-5}. $

papers.title: Dimension-seven spectator effects in charm-hadron lifetimes at NLO
papers.summary: We compute the next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections to the connected current-current part of the dimension-seven spectator coefficients in the heavy-quark expansion of charm-hadron widths. The finite terms are fixed in NDR-$\overline{\rm MS}$, with the evanescent operators defined by the standard Greek projection and averaged over Hermitian-conjugate pairs, and with a finite subtraction that sets the finite mixing of the dimension-seven operators into the dimension-six ones to zero. In several channels the one-loop term is comparable to the LO coefficient, and two operator families absent at LO are generated. Since the NLO matrix elements of the dimension-seven operators are not known, we estimate the effect of the coefficients on the widths with tree-level matrix elements from vacuum insertion for $D$ mesons and from the bag model for charmed baryons. The $1/m_c$ corrections to the matrix elements of the dimension-six QCD operators are treated by a naive expansion. Without their $O(α_s)$ part the semileptonic width of the $D_s^+$ would be negative. The NLO dimension-seven correction raises the $D^+$ width by 0.78 ps$^{-1}$, so that its central value, slightly negative as published, becomes positive. At central inputs, it is about 1% of the $D^0$ width, 10% of the $D_s^+$ width and at most 2% of the widths of the singly charmed baryons. Added to the published pole-scheme width, the $D^+$ correction gives $τ(D^+)=1.41^{+\infty}_{-0.76}$ ps. The NLO term reduces the scale dependence of the nonleptonic dimension-seven contribution severalfold for the singly charmed baryons, whose matrix elements are evolved, but not uniformly for the $D$ mesons.
papers.comments: 41 pages, 8 figures, 8 tables; Wilson coefficients and diagram-by-diagram code as ancillary files

papers.title: Colours and Flavours: ropes and colour reconnection as string multiplets
papers.summary: The increase of strange-hadron yields with event activity and the enhanced charm-baryon fractions in hadronic collisions motivate a microscopic examination of how the colour environment affects hadronization. We review and develop the string description of these effects, starting from the Lund fragmentation baseline in electron--positron annihilation and following colour correlations beyond the leading-colour approximation. Few-parton examples show how junction formation and rope hadronization arise from the same SU(3) colour structure, connecting baryon formation and the screening forces that govern strange-quark production. For nuclear collisions, we introduce a local escape criterion and a phenomenological saturation of the breakup force, motivated by a three-string example of screening through background colour correlations. With common settings, the combined prescription gives a satisfactory description of light-flavour ratios in pp and p--Pb and provides O--O predictions. Charm ratios reveal a substantial remaining deficit in $Ξ_c$ production, motivating separate tests of the fragmentation baseline and its extrapolation with activity.
papers.comments: 24 pages, submitted to the Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science

papers.title: Doubly strange tetraquark as a $KK^*$ virtual state: quark-model study with harmonic traps
papers.summary: We extract hadron--hadron scattering information from quark-level interactions using an artificial harmonic trap and a four-quark basis that includes both meson--meson and compact diquark--antidiquark configurations. Combining the Busch--Englert--Rzażewski--Wilkens formula with the effective range expansion (ERE), we determine phase shifts, scattering lengths, effective ranges, and pole positions from the trapped spectrum. We control uncertainties from basis truncation, finite trap frequencies, truncation of ERE, and quark-model parameters. The extracted $DD^*$ and $BB^*$ binding energies agree with direct calculations, providing benchmarks. For the doubly strange $T_{ss}$ with $I(J^P)=0(1^+)$, we predict a $KK^*$ virtual-state pole about 30--35~MeV below threshold in the stable-$K^*$ approximation. Both the AL1 model and its modified version that better reproduces the measured $T_{cc}^+$ binding energy yield this result. This finding differs from earlier predictions of a bound state and motivates searches for the $T_{ss}$ at facilities such as the High Intensity heavy Ion Accelerator Facility (HIAF). This framework could be extended to other hadron-hadron channels to extract scattering observables and pole positions.

papers.title: General Formulation of Covariant Tensor Amplitudes for Purely Hadronic and Single-photon Radiative Cascade Decays
papers.summary: We present a unified method for generating Lorentz-covariant partial-wave amplitudes for multi-body purely hadronic and single-photon radiative cascade decays within the covariant $L$-$S$ tensor formalism. Based on the structural decoupling of external polarization wave functions, complex coupling parameters, and the core covariant amplitude tensor $U$, we establish a hierarchical vertex contraction procedure that explicitly incorporates intermediate-state cascade bridge projection operators $P^{(J_i)}(p_i)$ and parent-frame definite-spin projection operators $P^{(S_{BC})}(p_A)$. This rigorous treatment guarantees the Rarita-Schwinger symmetry, tracelessness, and transversality conditions across different reference frames, fundamentally eliminating the unphysical longitudinal and trace contaminations induced by Lorentz boosts in cascade decays. Furthermore, we formulate a general covariant tensor representation for single-photon radiative decays $A(J_M) \to γ+ X(J_X)$ that strictly satisfies photon gauge invariance ($q^λV_{\dotsλ\dots} = 0$) in the Lorenz gauge. Built upon normal- and anomalous-parity fundamental transverse tensors ($K_{μν}$ and $S_{μν}$), universal recursive formulas are derived via the systematic replacement $g_{μν} \to q_μp_{Aν}$, accompanied by exact rules for matching the orbital angular momentum ranks of Blatt-Weisskopf centrifugal barrier factors $B_{L_{\text{rad}}}$ and a spectator index pass-through mechanism for the photon polarization index.

papers.title: Lean-Verified No-Go Theorems for $R$-Symmetries and Modular Symmetries in 4D GUTs
papers.summary: $R$-symmetries are instrumental in supersymmetric model building. However, a no-go theorem restricts us from using them in a large class of four-dimensional (4D) grand unified theories (GUTs). Specifically, it has been shown that a supersymmetric 4D GUT based on SU(5), with finitely many chiral multiplets, cannot be broken spontaneously to the exact minimal supersymmetric standard model (MSSM) while preserving a discrete $\mathbb{Z}_M^R$, with $M \geq 3$, or continuous U(1) $R$-symmetry. We use Lean 4 to formalize this proof. In the process, we identify and close a gap in the general case of the published argument. Further, we discuss the implications for GUT models with modular symmetries. We point out that modular symmetries are inevitably $R$-symmetries in a supersymmetric framework that also describes gravity. At certain critical points in moduli space, discrete $R$-symmetries are linearly realized. In the context of 4D GUTs, the no-go theorem then implies that exotic states become massless at these points, provided the GUT-breaking vacuum preserves these symmetries. In the vicinity of these critical points, these exotics are parametrically light, which may spoil gauge coupling unification.

papers.title: Strong Decays of the $2^-$ Heavy-Light Mesons in the Relativistic Bethe-Salpeter Approach
